findings.title: Unprocessable reminders never accumulate retries
findings.body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing, this condition skips the scheduling call without updating `retryCount` or deleting the reminder. Because the query selects unscheduled SMS reminders again on every cron run, these rows bypass the two-failure limit and are only removed when their scheduled date expires.

findings.title: Retry increments can be lost by overlapping cron runs
findings.body: The failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value read by `findMany`. If two cron requests process the same reminder concurrently, both can read the same count and overwrite it with the same next value, so multiple failed scheduling attempts count as one. The reminder can therefore be retried more than twice before reaching the deletion threshold; use an atomic increment and coordinate concurrent processing.
